Classic Mixed Berry Pie

Served at: Independence Day (United States)

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 50 min

Berry pie is a beloved dessert traditionally served on Independence Day in the United States, symbolizing the bounty of summer and the colors of the American flag with its vibrant red and blue hues. This classic mixed berry pie combines fresh strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries in a flaky homemade crust, making it a festive and delicious way to celebrate the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour (315 g), plus extra for dusting
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 tablespoon granulated sugar
  • 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  • 1/4 to 1/2 cup ice water
  • 1 tablespoon lemon juice
  • 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 1/4 cup cornstarch
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
  • 1 cup fresh blueberries
  • 1 cup fresh raspberries
  • 1 tablespoon butter, cut into small pieces
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • 1 tablespoon coarse sugar (optional, for topping)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, and sugar for the crust.
  2. Cut in the cold butter using a pastry cutter or your fingers until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
  3. Gradually add ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together.
  4. Divide the dough into two discs, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
  5. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
  6. In a large bowl, mix the berries with lemon juice, sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, and salt until well combined.
  7. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one dough disc into a 12-inch (30 cm) circle and fit it into a 9-inch (23 cm) pie dish.
  8. Pour the berry filling into the crust and dot with butter pieces.
  9. Roll out the second dough disc and place it over the filling. Trim excess dough and crimp edges to seal.
  10. Cut slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
  11. Brush the top crust with beaten egg and sprinkle with coarse sugar if desired.
  12. Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce heat to 350°F (175°C) and bake for an additional 30 minutes or until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbly.
  13. Allow the pie to cool for at least 2 hours before serving to let the filling set.

Tips

  • Use a mix of fresh berries for the best flavor and color.
  • If fresh berries are not available, frozen berries can be used but thaw and drain excess liquid before mixing.
  • For a decorative touch, cut shapes from the top crust dough or create a lattice crust instead of a solid top.
